Description: SSD introduced for residential properties sold within one year of purchase.
SSD holding period extended to three years for newly acquired residential properties.
SSD holding period extended to four years, with rates of 16%, 12%, 8% and 4%.
Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty rates were raised for multiple-property buyers, permanent residents, foreigners and entities.
MAS introduced the Total Debt Servicing Ratio framework for property loans.
SSD holding period shortened from four years to three years and rates reduced to 12%, 8% and 4%.
Top marginal Buyer's Stamp Duty rate for residential property increased from 3% to 4%.
ABSD rates were raised for Singapore citizens buying additional homes, permanent residents, foreigners and entities.
ABSD rates were raised, the TDSR threshold was tightened and housing loan limits were reduced.

Policy: HDB financing tightened and 15-month wait-out introduced
Description: HDB loan LTV was lowered and a 15-month wait-out period was imposed on private-property owners buying non-subsidised HDB resale flats.
Top marginal Buyer's Stamp Duty rate for residential property increased to 6%.
ABSD rates were raised, including the rate for foreigners buying residential property from 30% to 60%.
The LTV limit for HDB housing loans was lowered from 80% to 75%.
SSD holding period was restored to four years, with rates of 16%, 12%, 8% and 4%.
The wait-out period for private-property owners purchasing non-subsidised HDB resale flats was removed.
